**Tier 2** — canonical — the only tier humans edit · owned by `data-ingestion` · `public.demand_forecasts`

**One row is** One forecast BUCKET of one customer × product row: from `period_start`, for one week or one calendar month, this customer is expected to take `quantity` of this product (PLAN.md §24 WP 14.2, ADR 0002 decisions 2 and 7). A series is the row's buckets in date order. The plan reads it as the centre of the row's weekly demand; the simulated world draws actual demand around it.

## Uniqueness

| Columns | Source | Constraint |

| `id` | column PRIMARY KEY | `demand_forecasts_pkey` |
| `project_id` + `customer_id` + `product_id` + `period_start` | UNIQUE index | `demand_forecasts_natural_key` |

**Natural key:** `project_id` + `customer_id` + `product_id` + `period_start` — the key this table's grain implies, and the
database ENFORCES it: `demand_forecasts_natural_key`. A re-upload of the same row updates
it rather than duplicating it.

### `quantity`

How much the customer is forecast to take over the WHOLE bucket — 1 000 for a month is 1 000 over that month. Spread evenly over the bucket's days at promotion (decision 7) into `weekly_quantity`; nothing reads this column as a rate.

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | `numeric`, `NOT NULL` |
| Grain | `rate` |
| Unit | `units over the bucket` — column, named by `time_unit` |
| Added by | `20261003000001_demand_per_row.sql` |
| Read by the engine | `demand_forecast_spread() -> weekly_quantity` |
| Validated at ingest | numeric >= 0 |
| Rendered at | *not yet recorded (WP 5.1)* |

**Resolution** — how a value is decided when more than one source could supply one.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default mode | `asserted` |
| Assertable by | `csv_upload` |
| Estimable from | **never** — this value may not be estimated |
| Hybrid (centre / spread) | **none** — the engine has no variability field for this quantity |
| On conflict | `assertion_wins` |

A forecast is the user's statement of what they expect; it is not estimated here. History-based forecasting (P-F.1) is out of scope for Phase 14 (design doc §8).

> `unit_source: column` with NO `normalize_at_promotion`, deliberately. The generic `rate` conversion rewrites the unit column to `week`, which would erase the bucket's length; the conversion this column needs is the calendar spread `demand_forecast_spread()` applies in the promoting statement, which writes `period_end` and `weekly_quantity` and leaves `time_unit` as uploaded.
